note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Scope & Chargeability of Capital Gains
explain: Any profits or gains from transferring a capital asset during a tax year are taxable under 'Capital Gains'.
Tax liability generally arises in the tax year in which the transfer takes place.
The charging section requires two main components: a 'capital asset' and a 'transfer'.

flow.title: Capital Gains Chargeability Test
steps: Identify asset as a Capital Asset
Check if transaction qualifies as Transfer
Determine the Tax Year of Transfer
Tax in the Year of Transfer

topics.example: Selling a plot of land held as an investment in June 2026 creates a capital gain taxable in T.Y. 2026-27.
remember: Actual date of sale/transfer governs the tax year, not the date of agreement to sell.
mistakes: Taxing capital gains in the year money is received instead of the year the transfer happens.

quiz.q: Under Section 67(1), capital gains are generally charged to tax in the tax year in which:
o: Transfer of capital asset takes place
quiz.why: Capital gains accrue in the tax year in which the transfer actually takes place.

quiz.q: Which two essential elements must exist to attract tax under the head 'Capital Gains'?
quiz.why: Section 67 requires profits arising from the transfer of a capital asset.

topics.title: Definition of Capital Asset & Exclusions
explain: Capital asset means property of any kind held by an assessee, connected with business or not.
It includes securities held by Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) or specified investment funds.
Exclusions include stock-in-trade, personal effects (movables for personal use), rural agricultural land, and notified Gold Bonds.
Personal effects DO NOT exclude jewellery, drawings, paintings, sculptures, archaeological collections, and works of art (these are capital assets).

flow.title: Capital Asset Identification Process
steps: Verify if stock-in-trade or raw material
Check if movable property for personal use
Check if jewellery, art, or drawing

topics.example: A personal motor car is a personal effect and not a capital asset, but personal gold jewellery is a capital asset.
remember: Rural agricultural land is NOT a capital asset, but urban agricultural land IS a capital asset.
mistakes: Treating personal jewellery as a personal effect excluded from capital assets.

quiz.q: Which of the following is treated as a Capital Asset under Section 2(22)?
quiz.why: Jewellery is specifically excluded from personal effects and is treated as a capital asset.

quiz.q: Urban agricultural land is classified as:
quiz.why: Only rural agricultural land is excluded from capital assets; urban agricultural land is a capital asset.

topics.title: Short-Term vs Long-Term Capital Assets & Period of Holding
explain: Short-term capital asset (STCA) means an asset held for not more than 24 months preceding transfer date (12 months for listed securities, equity mutual funds, and zero-coupon bonds).
Long-term capital asset (LTCA) means an asset held for more than 24 months (or >12 months for 12-month category).
Under Section 76, market-linked debentures, unlisted bonds/debentures, and specified debt mutual funds acquired on/after 1.4.2023 are ALWAYS STCA.
topics.example: An unlisted share held for 15 months is an STCA (threshold 24m), but a listed share held for 15 months is an LTCA (threshold 12m).
remember: 12 Months: Listed securities, Equity-oriented funds, Zero Coupon Bonds.
24 Months: Unlisted shares, immovable properties, and other assets.
mistakes: Applying 36-month threshold which was replaced by 24 months for general unlisted assets and land/building.

quiz.q: An unlisted equity share becomes a Long-Term Capital Asset if held for more than:
quiz.why: Unlisted shares have a 24-month holding threshold under Section 2(101).

quiz.q: Under Section 76, gain on transfer of Market Linked Debentures is always treated as:
quiz.why: Section 76 overrides holding period rules to treat gains from market-linked debentures strictly as short-term.

topics.title: Definition & Scope of Transfer
explain: Transfer includes sale, exchange, or relinquishment of an asset.
Extinguishment of rights, compulsory acquisition under law, and conversion of capital asset into stock-in-trade are transfers.
Maturity or redemption of Zero Coupon Bonds is a transfer.
Part-performance of contract (Section 53A of Transfer of Property Act) and enabling enjoyment of immovable property (like co-op society flat allotment) count as transfer.

flow.title: Types of Transactions Qualifying as Transfer

topics.example: Handing over physical possession of a house under a sale agreement after receiving full price is a transfer, even before registration.
remember: Converting a personal asset into stock-in-trade is NOT taxable, but converting a capital asset into stock-in-trade IS a transfer.
mistakes: Believing that registration of sale deed is strictly required for income tax transfer rules to apply.

quiz.q: Which of the following constitutes a 'Transfer' under Section 2(109)?
o: Gift of asset by an individual
Conversion of capital asset into stock-in-trade
Partition of HUF asset in kind
quiz.why: Converting a capital asset into stock-in-trade is explicitly included in Section 2(109).

quiz.q: Redemption of Zero Coupon Bonds on maturity is treated as:
quiz.why: Section 2(109) includes maturity or redemption of zero coupon bonds in the definition of transfer.

topics.title: Special Year of Chargeability Rules
explain: Insurance Claims (Section 67(2)): Taxable in the year insurance money or asset is received upon damage/destruction by flood, fire, or riot.
Conversion to Stock-in-Trade (Section 67(6)): Transfer happens in year of conversion, but tax is charged in the year stock-in-trade is sold.
Compulsory Acquisition (Section 67(12)): Taxable in the year initial compensation (or part) is first received.
Enhanced compensation is taxable in the year received; interim court order amounts are taxable in the year final order is passed.

flow.title: Conversion to Stock-in-Trade Taxation Flow
steps: Transfer happens at Conversion date FMV
Capital Gain = FMV at conversion minus Cost
Business Income = Sale Price minus FMV at conversion
Tax both components in Year of Sale

topics.example: Shares converted to stock-in-trade in 2025-26 and sold in 2026-27: capital gains and business profits are both taxed in 2026-27.
remember: Compulsory acquisition original compensation is taxed on initial receipt basis, not transfer date.
mistakes: Taxing conversion of asset into stock-in-trade in the year of conversion instead of year of sale.

quiz.q: Capital gain on conversion of a capital asset into stock-in-trade is chargeable to tax in the tax year in which:
quiz.why: Section 67(6) defers chargeability to the tax year in which the converted stock is actually sold.

quiz.q: Compensation received under an interim court order for compulsory acquisition is taxable in the year of:
quiz.why: Under Section 67(12)(c), interim compensation is deemed income of the tax year when the final order is passed.

topics.title: Liquidation Distribution & Buyback of Shares
explain: Company Liquidation (Section 68): Distribution of specie assets by liquidated company is NOT a transfer in company hands.
Shareholders are taxed on money/asset FMV received minus accumulated profits deemed dividend under Section 2(40)(c).
Buyback of Shares (Section 69): Shareholder is taxed on buyback consideration minus cost of acquisition as capital gain.
Promoters selling in buyback pay additional tax (2% or 9.5% for domestic; 10% or 17.5% for non-domestic) plus 12% surcharge.

flow.title: Liquidation Tax Treatment for Shareholder
steps: Net Amount = Full Value of Consideration
Subtract Cost of Acquisition of shares

topics.example: Shareholder receives ₹10 lakhs assets on liquidation, including ₹2 lakhs accumulated profits. Full value of consideration for capital gains is ₹8 lakhs.
remember: Deemed dividend portion on liquidation is taxed under 'Income from Other Sources'.
mistakes: Including accumulated profits portion in full value of consideration for capital gains on liquidation.

quiz.q: Distribution of assets in specie to shareholders on liquidation is treated as:
o: Not a transfer in company's hands
quiz.why: Section 68(1) states distribution of specie assets on liquidation is not regarded as transfer by the company.

quiz.q: What flat surcharge rate applies to additional tax payable on buy-back of shares by promoters?
quiz.why: A flat surcharge @12% is levied on additional tax payable on buy-back of shares.

topics.title: Transactions Not Regarded as Transfer
explain: Section 70 lists specific transactions exempt from capital gains tax treatment.
Includes partition of HUF assets, gifts, wills, or irrevocable trust transfers.
Transfers between 100% parent and Indian subsidiary companies are exempt.
Amalgamation and demerger transfers of assets between Indian companies are exempt.
Conversions of bonds/debentures or preference shares into equity shares, and Reverse Mortgage transactions are NOT transfers.

flow.title: Exempt Transfer Check (Section 70)
steps: If yes to any, transaction is Not a Transfer

topics.example: Converting 100 preference shares into 100 equity shares of the same company does not trigger capital gains tax.
remember: Parent-subsidiary exemption applies ONLY if the transferee company is an Indian company.
mistakes: Taxing conversion of convertible debentures into equity shares at conversion time.

quiz.q: Which of the following transactions is regarded as a transfer liable to capital gains tax?
o: Distribution of assets on HUF partition
Transfer of capital asset under a Will
Conversion of preference shares into equity shares
Sale of land to an unrelated third party
quiz.why: Sale of land to a third party is a regular taxable transfer; the others are non-transfer transactions under Section 70.

quiz.q: For parent-subsidiary transfer exemption under Section 70, the subsidiary must be 100% owned and:
quiz.why: The transferee subsidiary or holding company must be an Indian company.

topics.title: Mode of Computation & Cost Inflation Index
explain: Capital Gain = Full Value of Consideration minus (Transfer Expenses + Cost of Acquisition + Cost of Improvement).
Securities Transaction Tax (STT) paid is NOT deductible from sale consideration.
Under Section 197 for resident individuals/HUF transferring land/building acquired before 23.7.2024, tax excess over 20% with indexation is ignored.
Indexation formula increases cost based on CII of transfer year over CII of acquisition year (or 2001-02).
topics.example: Selling property for ₹50 lakhs with ₹1 lakh brokerage gives Net Consideration of ₹49 lakhs.
remember: STT paid on purchase/sale of securities cannot be claimed as an expense.
mistakes: Deducting STT while calculating short-term or long-term capital gains on shares.

quiz.q: Which of the following expenses CANNOT be deducted from Full Value of Consideration?
quiz.why: Section 72 explicitly prohibits deduction of STT.

quiz.q: Base year for Cost Inflation Index (CII) in India with index value 100 starts from financial year:
quiz.why: The current CII base year set to 100 is F.Y. 2001-02.

topics.title: Ascertainment of Cost of Acquisition in Special Cases
explain: Gift/Inheritance: Cost to previous owner is deemed as cost of acquisition.
Assets acquired prior to 1.4.2001: Cost is higher of actual cost or FMV as on 1.4.2001 (for land/building FMV capped at Stamp Duty Value on 1.4.2001).
Bonus Shares: Allotted on/after 1.4.2001 = Nil; Allotted before 1.4.2001 = FMV on 1.4.2001.
Rights Shares: Amount actually paid to acquire rights shares.
Rights Entitlement renounced: Cost is Nil to renouncer; purchase price paid + company fee to buyer.

flow.title: Cost of Acquisition Decision Flow
steps: If Gift/Will, cost = previous owner cost
If acquired before 1.4.2001, option of 1.4.2001 FMV
If Land/Building, FMV capped at 1.4.2001 SDV
If Bonus share post 1.4.2001, cost = Nil

topics.example: Property bought in 1995 for ₹30,000, 1.4.2001 FMV ₹1.4 lakh, SDV ₹1.2 lakh. Cost of acquisition is ₹1.2 lakh.
remember: Stamp Duty Value as on 1.4.2001 acts as a upper limit cap on 1.4.2001 FMV for land and buildings.
mistakes: Taking FMV on 1.4.2001 higher than Stamp Duty Value on 1.4.2001 for real estate.

quiz.q: What is the cost of acquisition of bonus shares allotted on or after 1st April 2001?
quiz.why: Cost of acquisition for bonus shares allotted on or after 1.4.2001 is taken as Nil under Section 90.

quiz.q: For land bought in 1990, the FMV on 1.4.2001 is ₹10 lakhs and SDV on 1.4.2001 is ₹8 lakhs. The cost of acquisition is:
quiz.why: FMV on 1.4.2001 cannot exceed Stamp Duty Value as on 1.4.2001.

topics.title: Cost of Improvement Rules
explain: Cost of improvement includes capital expenditure incurred in making additions/alterations to the asset.
Goodwill of business/profession, brand names, or right to manufacture always have Cost of Improvement as NIL.
Any capital expenditure incurred before 1st April 2001 is IGNORED completely.
Capital expenditure incurred on or after 1.4.2001 by previous owner or assessee is included.
topics.example: Adding a floor to a building in 1998 for ₹1 lakh is ignored; adding a floor in 2005 for ₹3 lakhs is allowable Cost of Improvement.
remember: Expenditure deductible under House Property or PGBP cannot be claimed as Cost of Improvement.
mistakes: Including construction/improvement expenses incurred prior to 1.4.2001.

quiz.q: Cost of improvement incurred prior to 1st April 2001 is:
quiz.why: Section 90(1) ignores all capital improvement costs incurred before 1.4.2001.

quiz.q: What is the cost of improvement for self-generated goodwill of a business?
quiz.why: Cost of improvement for goodwill and intangible rights is taken as Nil.

topics.title: Depreciable Assets & Power Sector Assets
explain: Depreciable Assets (Section 74): Capital gains on transfer of depreciable assets forming part of a block are always STCG.
STCG arises if full value of consideration exceeds (Opening WDV + Cost of new assets acquired + Transfer expenses).
Short-term capital loss arises if all assets in the block are sold for less than WDV + additions.
If block continues to exist with at least one asset, no capital gain/loss arises unless sale consideration exceeds total block value.

flow.title: Depreciable Block Tax Outcome
steps: Total Cost (C) = Opening WDV + Additions + Expenses
Is V > C? -> STCG arises (V - C)
If V < C, Check if all assets sold
If all assets sold -> STCL arises (C - V)
If assets remain -> Closing WDV = C - V

topics.example: Block WDV ₹8.5 lakh, addition ₹8.5 lakh, 3 of 6 machines sold for ₹21 lakh. STCG = ₹21L - ₹17L = ₹4 lakh.
remember: Depreciable assets gains/losses under Section 74 are strictly Short-Term regardless of holding duration.
mistakes: Treating gain on a 5-year old depreciable machinery block as Long-Term Capital Gain.

quiz.q: Capital gain arising from the transfer of a depreciable asset forming part of a block is treated as:
quiz.why: Section 74 deems gains from block of depreciable assets as short-term capital gains.

quiz.q: A block of machinery has opening WDV ₹5 lakhs. All machines are sold during the year for ₹3 lakhs without new additions. What is the result?
quiz.why: When all assets in a block cease to exist and sale value is less than total WDV, STCL of ₹2 lakhs arises.

topics.title: Market Linked Debentures & Debt Mutual Funds
explain: Gains from transfer, redemption, or maturity of Specified Mutual Funds acquired on/after 1.4.2023 are always STCG.
Gains from Market Linked Debentures and unlisted bonds/debentures are always STCG.
Specified Mutual Fund means a fund investing >65% of total proceeds in debt and money market instruments.
STCG formula: X = A - B - C (Consideration minus Cost minus Transfer expenses); STT is not deductible.
topics.example: Unlisted debentures held for 5 years sold at a gain generate Short-Term Capital Gain under Section 76.
remember: Specified debt mutual funds must invest >65% in debt/money market instruments.
mistakes: Applying indexation or long-term tax rates to Market Linked Debentures held over 3 years.

quiz.q: A Specified Mutual Fund is one which invests more than what percentage in debt and money market instruments?
quiz.why: Definition under Section 76 requires more than 65% investment in debt and money market instruments.

quiz.q: Gains on unlisted debentures held for 4 years and redeemed in 2026 are taxed as:
o: Short-Term Capital Gains at normal rates
quiz.why: Under Section 76, unlisted debenture transfers always give rise to Short-Term Capital Gain.

topics.title: Slump Sale Computation
explain: Slump sale is transfer of one/more undertakings for a lump sum consideration without assigning values to individual assets/liabilities.
Holding period > 36 months gives LTCG (taxed @12.5%); <= 36 months gives STCG.
Deemed Cost of Acquisition = Net Worth of undertaking.
Net Worth = Aggregate book value of assets (WDV for depreciable; NIL for self-generated goodwill) minus book value of liabilities.
Deemed Consideration = Fair Market Value of undertaking/consideration under Rule 53 (higher of FMV1 or FMV2).

flow.title: Slump Sale Gain Calculation
steps: Determine FMV of Slump Sale (Higher of FMV1, FMV2)
Capital Gain = Net Consideration minus Net Worth

topics.example: Selling an undertaking for ₹25 lakhs with Net Worth ₹12.5 lakhs gives Capital Gain of ₹12.5 lakhs.
remember: Revaluation of assets is completely ignored when computing Net Worth.
mistakes: Using revalued asset figures instead of book values/WDV while computing Net Worth.

quiz.q: Under Section 77, what is deemed to be the cost of acquisition for a slump sale?
o: Book value of fixed assets only
quiz.why: Section 77(3)(a) deems the net worth of the undertaking as cost of acquisition.

quiz.q: While calculating Net Worth for slump sale, revaluation of assets is:
quiz.why: Section 77(5) explicitly requires ignoring any change due to revaluation of assets.

topics.title: Deemed Full Value of Consideration
explain: Real Estate (Section 78): If Stamp Duty Value (SDV) > 110% of consideration, SDV is deemed full value of consideration.
Agreement Date SDV applies if part consideration was received on/before agreement date via specified banking/online mode.
Unquoted Shares (Section 79): If sale consideration < FMV determined under rules, FMV is deemed consideration.
Unascertainable Consideration (Section 80): If consideration cannot be determined, FMV of asset on transfer date is deemed consideration.

flow.title: Section 78 Stamp Duty Safe Harbor Test
steps: Check banking payment date for Agreement SDV eligibility

topics.example: Property sold for ₹100 lakhs, SDV is ₹108 lakhs (<=110%). Full value of consideration is actual ₹100 lakhs.
remember: Safe harbor limit for land/building stamp duty value tolerance is 110% (10% variation allowance).
mistakes: Taking registration date SDV when banking advance was paid on agreement date.

quiz.q: Under Section 78, Stamp Duty Value becomes full consideration only if it exceeds actual consideration by more than:
quiz.why: If SDV > 110% of actual consideration, SDV is taken as deemed full value of consideration.

quiz.q: If consideration for transferring a capital asset is not ascertainable, Section 80 deems full value of consideration as:
o: FMV of asset on date of transfer
quiz.why: Section 80 prescribes FMV of asset on transfer date when consideration cannot be determined.

topics.title: Advance Money Received & Forfeited
explain: Advance received and forfeited BEFORE 1st April 2014 reduces Cost of Acquisition while calculating capital gains.
Advance received and forfeited ON OR AFTER 1st April 2014 is taxed under 'Income from Other Sources' u/s 92(2)(h) / 56(2)(ix).
Forfeited advance on or after 1.4.2014 DOES NOT reduce cost of acquisition.
Advance forfeited by a previous owner does NOT reduce the cost of acquisition for the current owner.

flow.title: Advance Forfeiture Treatment Decision
steps: If YES -> Deduct from Cost of Acquisition
If YES -> Tax under Income from Other Sources
Do NOT deduct post-2014 forfeiture from Cost

topics.example: Forfeited ₹1 lakh advance in 2010 reduces COA; forfeited ₹2 lakhs advance in 2018 is taxed as Other Sources in 2018 and COA remains unchanged.
remember: Only advances forfeited prior to 1-4-2014 reduce the cost of acquisition.
mistakes: Reducing cost of acquisition for advances forfeited after 1.4.2014.

quiz.q: Advance money received and forfeited during negotiations on 10th May 2018 is:
o: Taxed under Income from Other Sources
quiz.why: Advances forfeited on or after 1.4.2014 are taxable under 'Income from Other Sources'.

quiz.q: If an advance was forfeited by the previous owner before 1.4.2014, how does it affect the buyer who inherited the asset?
o: Does not reduce current buyer's cost
quiz.why: Advance forfeited by a previous owner does not go to reduce cost of acquisition of the current assessee.

topics.title: Capital Gains Deductions
explain: Section 82: Transfer of residential house; invest in 1 residential house (2 if LTCG <= ₹2 crore). Max cap ₹10 crore.
Section 83: Transfer of urban agricultural land; invest in new agricultural land within 2 years.
Section 84: Compulsory acquisition of industrial land/building; invest in industrial land/building within 3 years.
Section 85: Transfer of land/building; invest LTCG in NHAI/RECL/notified bonds within 6 months (Max ₹50 lakhs).
Section 86: Transfer of LTCA (other than residential house); invest Net Consideration in 1 residential house. Max cap ₹10 crore.
Unutilized CGAS deposits become taxable after 2/3 year period expires.

flow.title: Section 85 Investment Flow
steps: Deduction = Lower of Gain or Investment

topics.example: LTCG on land ₹75 lakhs, invested ₹50 lakhs in NHAI bonds within 5 months. Deduction under Section 85 is capped at ₹50 lakhs.
remember: Section 85 maximum bond investment limit is ₹50 lakhs in aggregate across financial years for a transfer.
mistakes: Claiming Section 85 deduction for investing in bonds after 6 months from transfer date.

quiz.q: Under Section 85, what is the maximum deduction allowed for investment in specified bonds?
quiz.why: Section 85 restricts maximum investment in specified bonds to ₹50 lakhs.

quiz.q: To claim deduction under Section 85, investment in NHAI/RECL bonds must be made within how many months from transfer date?
quiz.why: Section 85 requires investment in long-term specified bonds within 6 months after the transfer date.

topics.title: Reference to Valuation Officer
explain: Assessing Officer (AO) may refer valuation of a capital asset to a Valuation Officer to ascertain FMV.
Allowed if value claimed by assessee based on registered valuer estimate varies from AO's estimate.
Allowed if AO opinions FMV exceeds claimed value by more than prescribed percentage or nature of asset requires it.
If Valuation Officer's value < SDV, AO takes Valuation Officer's value; if Valuation Officer's value > SDV, SDV is retained.

flow.title: Valuation Reference Procedure
steps: AO refers asset to Valuation Officer
Compare Valuation Officer Value with SDV
Take lower of Valuation Officer Value and SDV

topics.example: SDV ₹50 lakhs, Valuation Officer determines ₹45 lakhs. AO adopts ₹45 lakhs as deemed sale consideration.
remember: Valuation Officer's report can reduce stamp duty valuation adopted by AO, but cannot increase it beyond SDV.
mistakes: Adopting Valuation Officer's value when it turns out to be higher than Stamp Duty Value.

quiz.q: Under Section 91, the Assessing Officer can refer an asset to a Valuation Officer to ascertain its:
quiz.why: Section 91 provides for reference to Valuation Officer for ascertaining fair market value.

quiz.q: If the Valuation Officer estimates value lower than Stamp Duty Value, the Assessing Officer shall adopt:
quiz.why: When Valuation Officer's valuation is lower than SDV, the lower valuation by Valuation Officer is adopted.

topics.title: Tax Rates on Capital Gains
explain: Section 196 (STCG on Listed Equity/Equity Funds): Taxable @ 20% if STT paid.
Section 197 (General LTCG): Taxable @ 12.5% on transfer of long-term capital assets.
Section 198 (LTCG on Listed Equity/Equity Funds): Gains exceeding ₹1,25,000 taxable @ 12.5% if STT paid.
Resident individuals/HUF can set off unexhausted basic exemption limit against STCG u/s 196 and LTCG u/s 197/198.
No Chapter VIII deductions allowed against capital gains taxed u/s 196, 197, or 198.

flow.title: Capital Gains Tax Rate Selection
steps: Is it STCG on Listed Equity (STT paid)? -> 20% u/s 196
Is it LTCG on Listed Equity (STT paid)? -> 12.5% over ₹1.25L u/s 198
Is it LTCG on Other Assets? -> 12.5% u/s 197
Is it STCG on Other Assets? -> Normal Slab Rates
Adjust unexhausted basic exemption for Resident Ind/HUF

topics.example: Resident LTCG u/s 198 is ₹2,00,000. Exempt amount ₹1,25,000, balance ₹75,000 taxed @ 12.5%.
remember: Section 198 provides an annual tax-free threshold of ₹1,25,000 on equity LTCG.
mistakes: Claiming Chapter VIII deductions (like Section 80C) against LTCG or STCG on equity shares.

quiz.q: What is the tax rate under Section 196 for short-term capital gains on STT-paid listed equity shares?
quiz.why: Section 196 taxes STCG on listed equity shares with STT paid at a concessional rate of 20%.

quiz.q: Under Section 198, LTCG on listed equity shares is exempt up to what threshold per tax year?
quiz.why: Section 198 levies tax @ 12.5% only on LTCG exceeding ₹1,25,000.
